newsitem.title: INDIA: Strike hits petrol stations in northern India.
newsitem.headline: Strike hits petrol stations in northern India.

text.p: Petrol stations run by private retailers in northern India were closed on Monday due to a day-long strike, a spokesman for the striking union said.

The strike was called by the All India Petroleum Dealers Association to press for a rise in sales commission to five percent from one percent, B.S. Suri, president of the union's Delhi wing, told Reuters.

The association also wants petroleum products excluded from the Essential Commodities Act, which allows government control on supply of key consumer goods, and compensation for product losses arising from temperature variations, Suri said.
Under India's state-controlled pricing regime, the government appoints dealers to sell petrol and gives them fixed commissions on their sales.
